# What a Skill Is

A directory with a `SKILL.md`: frontmatter that says **when** to use it, then Markdown instructions, optionally scripts and reference files beside it.

--

The body loads only when invoked, by you (`/name`) or by Claude when the request matches the description.

--

That is why a skill is the right home for a **multi-step procedure**:

- costs nothing until needed (module 4's lever)
- can carry a script, run through its own directory
- shareable through the repo, and installable as a plugin

--

Module 5 ended with "a procedure does not belong in memory." This is where it goes.

---
name: locations

# Where Skills Live

| Location | Path | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **Personal** | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | every project on this machine |
| **Project** | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | this repo, including cloud sessions |
| Nested | `<subdir>/.claude/skills/<name>/` | sessions started in or below `<subdir>` |
| Plugin | `<plugin>/skills/<name>/` | where the plugin is enabled; `/plugin:name` |
| Enterprise | managed settings directory | every user in the organization |

--

Same name in several places: enterprise beats personal beats project. Plugin skills are namespaced and never collide.

`.claude/commands/deploy.md` (the older custom command) still works and makes the same `/deploy`; skills add supporting files and invocation control. New work goes in skills.

---
name: anatomy

# Anatomy

```yaml
---
name: trip-report
description: Produce the per-city trip report from data/trips.csv. Use when the
  user says "trip report", "city summary", or asks how fares compare across cities.
argument-hint: [city]
allowed-tools: Bash(Rscript ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/report.R *)
---

Run `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/report.R $ARGUMENTS` and show the output.
If no city was given, report all cities. Do not edit the script.
```

--

Three lines do the work: `description` decides **whether** it loads, `allowed-tools` decides **what runs without a prompt**, and `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` makes the script path **portable** to wherever the skill is installed.

---

# The Fields That Control Invocation

| Frontmatter | You can invoke | Claude can invoke | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| (default) | yes | yes | most procedures |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | yes | no | side effects you start by hand: deploy, push, send |
| `user-invocable: false` | no | yes | background knowledge Claude applies unasked |

--

Also:

- `allowed-tools`: runs without a permission prompt during the invoking turn; does not restrict other tools. `disallowed-tools` removes tools while active.
- `context: fork` + `agent: Explore`: run in a subagent; output stays out of the main window.
- `paths:`: globs that limit automatic loading to work on matching files.
- `model`, `effort`, `hooks`: per-skill overrides.

---
name: arguments

# Arguments and Substitutions

| Placeholder | Expands to |
|---|---|
| `$ARGUMENTS` | everything typed after the name |
| `$0`, `$1` | positional, 0-based |
| `$city` | named, from an `arguments:` list in the frontmatter |
| `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` | the skill's own directory (works in `allowed-tools` too) |
| `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` | the project root |

--

`/trip-report Denver` → `$ARGUMENTS` is `Denver`. Multi-word values need quotes. Arguments with no placeholder to land in are appended as `ARGUMENTS: ...`.

--

A <code>!&#96;command&#96;</code> line (an exclamation mark, then the command in backticks) runs **before** the content is sent and inserts its output: a `git status --short` at the top of a commit skill, say.

--

Supporting files: `SKILL.md` under 500 lines as the overview; `reference.md`, `examples.md`, `scripts/` beside it, opened only when the overview points at them.

---
name: decision

# Skill, Memory, or Hook?

| Need | Mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a fact or rule for every task | `CLAUDE.md` | always loaded; cheap if short |
| a multi-step procedure for one kind of task | **skill** | on demand; carries scripts; shareable |
| something that must happen whatever Claude decides | hook (module 7) | the harness runs it; the rest is advice |
| a change to the interface or the harness | mod (module 8) | code, not instructions |

--

**Memory entry → skill** when it has numbered steps, names more than one command, or has outgrown a paragraph.

**Skill → hook** when it begins "always" or "never" and the cost of Claude skipping it is high.

---
name: description

# Writing a Description That Triggers

Claude matches the request against descriptions. The listing truncates `description` + `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters, key use case first.

--

.pull-left[
**Rarely fires**

```yaml
description: Slide verification helper.
```
]

.pull-right[
**Fires**

```yaml
description: Render a xaringan deck, print it
  to PDF, rasterize pages and read them back
  for overflow. Use when the user says "verify
  the slides", "spot-check slide N", or after
  any edit to a slides.Rmd. Not for the
  interview-prep .md, which uses make.
```
]

--

Action and object first, then **the triggers as things the user actually says**, then exclusions if a sibling skill is close.

Test both ways: `/name`, and a request phrased like a trigger without the name.

---
name: lifecycle

# Lifecycle

**1. Write it.** Creating `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` registers it **live** in the current session (observed 2026-07), sometimes a turn later. Smoke-test in the same conversation; if `Skill` says "unknown skill" once, follow the steps by hand.

--

**2. Smoke-test both invocations.** `/name arg`, then a natural request.

--

**3. Move the scripts in.** Anything run more than once goes in `scripts/`, called through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.

--

**4. Decide the scope.** Personal if it depends on this machine (sandbox paths, Ghostscript, `pbcopy`). Project if a collaborator or a cloud session needs it. An account-uploaded skill syncs down as `anthropic-skills:<name>`: upload only variants that do not exist locally, or you get two skills with one trigger.

--

**5. Share as a plugin** when others should install it: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` beside `skills/`, listed in a `marketplace.json`; `/plugin install name --marketplace owner/repo`. Module 8 shows the layout.

---

# Three Skills in This Collection Worth Reading

**`new-module`**: inputs to confirm in one batch, a pre-flight check against the spec with a **stop condition** ("if the module is not in the plan, surface it and stop"), explicit do-nots, a report format.

--

**`verify-slides`**: one chained bash call so the user sees one operation, then a **read-back checklist** (cut-off content, literal LaTeX, missing title) and a table of symptom → cause → fix. A procedure, not a command alias.

--

**`msr-lg`**: a trigger token that is itself the go-ahead ("do not ask whether to proceed"), a de-personalization rule for what gets written, and an offer of a handoff note at the end.

--

The pattern across all three: the skill encodes the **judgment** around the commands, not just the commands.

---

# Summary

| Do | Because |
|---|---|
| Put procedures in skills, facts in `CLAUDE.md` | on-demand loading; memory is paid every request |
| Write triggers as quoted user phrases | Claude matches the request against the description |
| Call scripts through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` | portable across personal, project and plugin scope |
| `allowed-tools` for the one command the skill runs | no permission prompt for the expected call, nothing else widened |
| `disable-model-invocation` for side effects | deploy, push, send start by hand |
| Smoke-test by name and by phrase, same session | it registers live |
| Project scope for anything a cloud session needs | the cloud never sees `~/.claude` |

--

The drill writes `trip-report` with a bundled script and exercises every row, ending by moving it to project scope.
